title: Lunar south-pole analog study
ai_disclosure: The supplied team document attributes its analysis scripts and text to Claude assistance with team review. This website integration was implemented with Codex assistance; provisional choices remain labelled for team review.

retired.name: Precision landing
retired.reason: Removed from this study: 1-5 m terrestrial terrain is unavailable and its terrain features overlap M4.

retired.name: Regolith operations
retired.reason: Removed from scoring: grain-size classes cannot discriminate the sites, spectral references fail the control test, and the missing-data score intervals overlap. Archived code and results remain available.

features.name: Equinox noon solar elevation
features.note: 90 - absolute latitude. This is the PDF's equinox geometric proxy, not annual maximum elevation or the actual lunar solar angle.

features.name: Fraction of daylight below 10 degrees
features.note: Annual ten-minute geometric solar calculation; sunrise threshold -0.833 degrees; no terrain horizon.

features.name: Longest continuous annual darkness
features.note: Circular annual night run at ten-minute spacing. The 120 h anchor is a team test requirement, not lunar night duration.

features.name: Annual minimum 2 m air temperature
features.note: Team-reported 2014-2023 reanalysis summary. Air temperature is a proxy for a surface thermal test.

features.name: Mean daily 2 m air-temperature range
features.note: Team-reported air-temperature range; not a measured lunar or terrestrial surface-temperature waveform.

features.name: Slope histogram overlap
features.note: Six slope bins, with a final bin above 30 degrees. The team CSV reports 30 m-grid statistics; raw DEM windows are not included in that archive.

features.name: Elevation range in a 16 km window
features.note: Reference relief is the team-reported 2477 m Connecting Ridge value. A factor of two gives exp(-0.5).

features.name: Annual mean 2 m air temperature
features.note: An Earth-achievable cold-environment anchor; not annual lunar ground temperature.

features.name: Annual maximum 2 m air temperature
features.note: Correlated with annual mean temperature. The thermal-block option shares half the M6 weight between the two temperatures.

features.name: Permafrost and subsurface-ice evidence
features.note: Only assessments explicitly listed in the PDF enter at c=0.3; other sites remain unknown. Component-level supporting literature is unverified. The optional temperature proxy cannot establish cold-trap ice.

assumptions: Anchors and weights are team proposals. Scores describe Earth-achievable test environments, not physical equivalence to the Moon.
Feature importance and uncertainty values were not supplied. Features use equal weights within each test unless the M6 thermal-block option is selected.
The four rounded PDF ROC weights are retained exactly. Selecting fewer tests renormalizes only those test weights.
The current slope and relief reference is Connecting Ridge only. Scores must not be relabelled as another lunar target.
A score based on available evidence is shown alongside completeness and data fitness. Missing data is never a measured zero.
Astronomical features ignore terrain obstruction. Air temperatures do not reproduce lunar surface temperatures, vacuum or one-sixth gravity.
Reported validation results are preliminary team results. Their original climate API responses and DEM processing windows were not included.

global_scan.stage1: Astronomy, POWER climatological mean temperature, coarse 16 km relief and an explicit temperature-based frozen-ground proxy.
global_scan.stage2: Refine the top 20 non-ice candidates plus the 15 validation locations using point climate summaries and 30 m terrain.
global_scan.ice_policy: Permanent ice-cover screening requires annual-maximum temperature or a verified ice-cover product. Annual mean alone cannot identify ice sheets.
